entry.name: overdrive~
entry.description: The overdrive~ object uses a waveshaping function to distort audio signals. It amplifies signals, limiting the maximum value of the signal to +/- 1. Values outside of this range are removed using "soft clipping" somewhat like that of an overdriven tube-based circuit.

arguments.name: drive-factor
arguments.description: A single number can be provided to set the drive factor. If no argument is provided, the drive factor is set to 1.0.

messages.name: float
messages.description: In right inlet: Theobject accepts a floating-point "drive factor". The drive factor should usually be in the range 1.0-10.0. Using a factor of 1.0 creates a linear response without distortion, and higher values increase the distortion. Values less than 1, including negative values, produce very heavily distorted signals. Use with caution, this behavior was originally considered a bug until friends of the object's creator insisted that it should be considered a feature and left intact.)

messages.name: int
messages.description: Integer inputs are converted toand set the drive factor. The drive factor should usually be in the range 1 - 10. Using a factor of 1 creates a linear response without distortion, and higher values increase the distortion. Values less than 1, including negative values, produce very heavily distorted signals. Use with caution.
